explain.say: In 1345, in a cathedral library in Verona, the poet Petrarch found letters by the Roman orator Cicero that had been lost for centuries. He was so moved he wrote letters back to Cicero. That passion for ancient texts is called humanism. Look at the timeline of the movement.

explain.say: Humanists studied what they called the studia humanitatis: grammar, rhetoric, poetry, history and moral philosophy. That is where the word humanities comes from. They hunted manuscripts, corrected copying errors and wrote elegant classical Latin. Why would correcting old texts matter so much?

explain.say: Here is humanism as a weapon. Watch the chain. The Donation of Constantine claimed the emperor had given the pope rule over the West. In 1440 Lorenzo Valla showed its Latin used words and ideas unknown in Constantine's time, so it was a later forgery. You do the same when you spot a fake quote online. Which link is the giveaway?

explain.say: Now the map. Greek scholars came to Italy, especially after Constantinople fell in 1453, bringing Plato and other texts. In Mainz, Gutenberg's press printed a Bible around 1455, and soon cities like Venice were printing ancient works by the thousand. How does printing change who can read the classics?

Was it a rebirth? See the debate. In 1860 Jacob Burckhardt saw modern individualism born in Italy. Critics point to a twelfth-century renaissance, medieval continuity and, with Jack Goody, many renaissances worldwide. Great work. Challenge: apply Valla's test to one claim you read this week.

faq.a: A movement, from fourteenth-century Italy, to revive and study the language, literature and ideas of ancient Greece and Rome through the studia humanitatis: grammar, rhetoric, poetry, history and moral philosophy.

faq.q: How did Lorenzo Valla prove the Donation of Constantine was fake?
faq.a: In 1440 Valla showed that its Latin contained words and usages, such as Roman officials called satraps, that did not exist in the fourth century, and that no contemporary source mentioned the gift. It was a forgery, probably from the eighth century.
asks: What was the Donation of Constantine?

faq.q: Was the Renaissance really a rebirth?
faq.a: Partly. Jacob Burckhardt, in 1860, saw a sharp break and the birth of the modern individual. Later historians stress medieval continuity, earlier revivals such as the twelfth-century renaissance, and similar revivals in other civilisations.
Printing with movable type, developed by Gutenberg in Mainz around 1450, made texts cheaper, standardised and widely available, so humanist editions of classical works spread across Europe quickly.
asks: Who invented the printing press in Europe?

faq.a: Desiderius Erasmus of Rotterdam, the leading northern humanist, who published an edition of the Greek New Testament in 1516 and satirised Church abuses while remaining Catholic.

facts: Petrarch found Cicero's letters to Atticus in Verona in 1345.
Lorenzo Valla wrote his exposure of the Donation of Constantine in 1440.
Jacob Burckhardt published The Civilization of the Renaissance in Italy in 1860.
